13 — SEO Checklist#

Check discoverability, crawl/index controls, content quality, usability, and measurement for sites meant to appear in search results.

Scope: Frontend-specific. This file is one part of the 13_SEO.md checklist. Apply the domain-wide release gate across all applicable scope files; each checklist ID remains unique.

Review details#

  • Project / product:
  • Release / version / environment:
  • Scope and applicable jurisdictions / markets:
  • Reviewer / owner:
  • Review date:
  • Decision: Pending / Approved / Approved with documented exceptions / Blocked

How to use#

  1. Copy this template into each project's review records; keep the shared repository template unchecked.
  2. Check [x] only after verifying the item with evidence. For any inapplicable item, record N/A and the reason in the project's own review notes or issue tracker using its checklist ID; do not mark it as passed.
  3. Record evidence links or artifact references by checklist ID. Open an issue for every failed item, assign an owner and due date, and retest after remediation.
  4. Apply the release gate below. These checklists guide review; they do not replace qualified specialist review when required.

Goals, audience, and content plan#

  • SEO-005 Navigation and information architecture make important pages easy to find.

  • SEO-001 Target audiences, markets, languages, priority pages, and conversion goals are documented.

  • SEO-002 For priority services and topics, map actual audience questions and distinct search intents to an appropriate primary page and useful supporting pages; identify relevant contextual internal links without keyword stuffing, compulsory article counts, or creating overlapping pages merely to target variants.

  • SEO-003 Each important page serves a distinct purpose and provides original, accurate, maintained content.

  • SEO-004 Content ownership, independent editorial review, factual sources, and update cadence are assigned. Where AI tools generate or substantially rewrite public pages or SEO metadata, verify an accountable reviewer fact-checks originality, accuracy, source rights, titles/descriptions, schema and image alt text before publishing. Numeric search volumes, clicks, rankings, pricing, traffic and research claims in AI-assisted reports must be attributable to authorized tools or actual fetched sources with a date and scope; mark unavailable values not checked rather than estimating from the model. Neither an agent's readiness score nor its asserted tool result substitutes for review approval.

  • SEO-033 Map editorial intent to canonical destination URLs and eliminate overlapping pages without distinct value.

  • SEO-034 Review content freshness for facts dependent on pricing, availability, laws, and time-sensitive product updates.

  • SEO-035 Document metadata and canonical rules for dynamically generated page types.

  • SEO-084 For sites with automatically assembled or data/template-driven page collections, verify the source dataset's rights, accuracy, required fields and update schedule; test representative, duplicate, incomplete and stale data rows for distinct, independently useful, fact-checked page content, working links, and accurate canonical/indexing and metadata signals. Exclude or appropriately noindex thin, repetitive, misleading or doorway-style variants rather than mass-publishing keyword substitutions.

Crawlability and indexation#

  • SEO-013 Site rendering exposes essential text and navigation to crawlers, including JavaScript-heavy pages; test initial and crawler-rendered HTML on representative routes and use server-side or static rendering when necessary rather than mandating SSR for every site.

  • SEO-036 Inspect live URL samples in Search Console to verify actual fetched HTML, rendering, and indexability.

  • SEO-037 Ensure JavaScript route links are real anchor elements with crawlable href values, not hash-only navigation.

  • SEO-006 Production pages intended for search are accessible to search-engine crawlers without unintended blocks.

  • SEO-007 robots.txt expresses deliberate crawling rules and does not accidentally block required resources; confirm Disallow only manages crawling, not privacy or guaranteed deindexing, and protect confidential material with authentication.

  • SEO-009 XML sitemaps list canonical, indexable URLs and are submitted where useful.

  • SEO-010 Canonical tags resolve duplicate/parameter variants consistently with intended URLs.

  • SEO-011 Internal links use descriptive anchor text and lead to working, relevant pages.

  • SEO-012 Redirects, broken links, soft 404s, and redirect chains are reviewed.

  • SEO-039 Confirm pagination links expose discoverable URLs rather than infinite-scroll-only content.

Technical experience and performance#

  • SEO-021 Mobile usability and responsive design work across supported devices.

  • SEO-024 HTTPS, browser security basics, and safe mixed-content behavior are verified.

  • SEO-025 Accessible navigation, semantic markup, and usable interactions support page quality.

  • SEO-026 Pagination, faceted navigation, infinite scroll, and filtering avoid unwanted index bloat where applicable.

  • SEO-044 Check for cumulative layout shifts from delayed images, fonts, banners, and dynamic data loads.

  • SEO-022 Core Web Vitals and real-user performance are measured; material issues have owners.

  • SEO-023 Images, fonts, scripts, and caching are optimized without breaking functionality.

  • SEO-043 Assess LCP, INP, and CLS at the 75th percentile for mobile and desktop, with regression budgets.

  • SEO-045 Verify that cookie dialogs, scripts, and heavy widgets do not obscure primary content or degrade core interactions.

On-page metadata and semantics#

  • SEO-014 Priority pages have unique, descriptive titles and useful meta descriptions. Before changing a low-CTR title, inspect the actual page–query pair, user intent, impressions, average position, search appearance, device and date range; compare the title shown in Google with the visible headline. Test truthful title improvements and track subsequent clicks, CTR and conversions without assuming Google will display the supplied title or that a title edit guarantees traffic.
  • SEO-015 Each page has a clear primary heading and logical subheading hierarchy.
  • SEO-016 URLs are readable, stable, and consistent about protocol, hostname, and trailing slashes.
  • SEO-017 Images have useful alternative text where appropriate and are delivered efficiently.
  • SEO-018 Structured data uses supported types, matches visible content, and passes relevant validation.
  • SEO-019 Hreflang annotations and language/region targets are correct where multilingual or regional versions exist.
  • SEO-020 Open Graph and other sharing metadata are accurate where relevant.
  • SEO-040 Verify structured-data properties and values are complete, accurate, and match visible content.
  • SEO-041 Test canonical, alternate-language, and social metadata across templates and locales.

Trust, measurement, and maintenance#

  • SEO-027 Organization details, authorship, contact information, and policies are accurate and discoverable.
  • SEO-083 For an eligible local or service-area business, verify the claimed business profile and relevant maintained listings reflect its real-world name, category, location or service area, hours, website and contacts; assign ownership for legitimate review responses and profile updates, and avoid duplicate or ineligible profiles.
  • SEO-085 For an eligible news publisher considering Google Preferred Sources, confirm its domain/subdomain appears in the current source preferences tool; if inviting readers to add it, verify the official button or deeplink uses the correct eligible site and works with accessible, voluntary user choice, without implying Publisher Center enrollment, a follower quota, guaranteed Top Stories appearance or daily traffic.
  • SEO-087 For creators or businesses tracking their own supported social/video accounts on Google Search, verify each applicable Instagram, TikTok, X or YouTube account/channel through its distinct Search Console platform property (or appropriate authorized owner access), confirm the correct account and connection status, and inspect available post/query-level Google Search performance with date, country and surface filters; distinguish Google Search/Discover/News clicks, impressions and reported positions from in-platform views, all-source traffic, website visits, conversions and sales. Record unavailable/partial reports without treating property creation, a keyword-led post or social sharing as a guarantee of indexing, rankings or revenue.
  • SEO-028 Claims and citations are verifiable; no misleading, mass-produced, or manipulative SEO content is used.
  • SEO-029 Verify ownership, correct site/property resolution, authorized access, and representative URL-inspection and sitemap-processing diagnostics in webmaster tools for the search engines actually targeted (such as Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools). For new or materially updated owned URLs, optionally request a crawl through the supported URL Inspection workflow; avoid automatic weekly resubmission of unchanged pages or assuming a seven-day indexing deadline. For AI-agent/MCP integrations, use least-privilege read scopes by default, separately approve supported write/URL-submission actions and verify eligible URLs; neither sitemap nor URL submission guarantees crawling, indexing, ranking or a faster recrawl.
  • SEO-030 Analytics tracks agreed search goals with privacy-compliant consent and data handling.
  • SEO-031 Assign an owner and evidence-based review cadence for indexing, crawl errors, query impressions/clicks/CTR, important landing pages, and conversions. On owned Search Console properties, optionally segment long-tail, question and commercial/comparison queries using RE2 filters (for example, best, versus, alternatives, pricing, cost and reviews). Verify page–query relevance, typical position, search appearance, device, dates and sample size before revising content or titles. Distinguish estimated keyword demand from observed impressions, clicks and actual customers; account for omitted/anonymized queries and truncated reports. Do not infer AI citations or require arbitrary page output, position thresholds, seven-day cycles or publishing quotas. Verify any rank-monitoring provider, query source, automation and permissions comply with search policies; prefer authorized webmaster analytics over unapproved automated SERP scraping.
  • SEO-032 For site redesigns or migrations that change URLs, inventory important existing URLs and search/referral baselines before launch, approve old-to-new URL mappings or intentional removals, assign owners, and monitor new and old URL crawl/index status and organic traffic after launch. For eligible domain/subdomain moves, verify required old/new properties and use the Search Console Change of Address process where applicable; do not apply it to path-only changes, HTTP-to-HTTPS changes, or www/non-www switches on the same domain. Do not require redirects when URLs remain unchanged.
  • SEO-046 Before implementing or changing schema for a desired Google search appearance, verify that the specific rich-result feature remains supported and applicable to the page, validate the markup and relevant Search Console enhancement reports, and do not promise retired features (such as FAQ, HowTo or sitelinks search-box results) or mistake valid Schema.org vocabulary for Google rich-result eligibility.
  • SEO-086 For launches, template/CMS updates, migrations and AI-assisted publishing that could affect organic discovery, capture a versioned pre-release and post-release sample of high-value and representative production URLs. Compare actual response and redirect targets, robots.txt and HTTP X-Robots-Tag/meta index directives, canonical URLs, sitemap entries, rendered essential content and relevant schema, including the intended production hostname; alert or block rollout on unapproved search-critical regressions (for example, an indexable 200 becoming noindex, 404, an unrelated canonical or sitewide bot block), identify the owner and confirm rollback or remediation with a fresh live test. Keep intentional exclusions and changes documented; do not treat snapshots as proof of Google indexing.
  • SEO-047 Investigate large indexing or traffic changes by release and page type, not ranking estimates alone.
  • SEO-048 For redesigned or migrated URLs, validate sampled and high-value old-to-new mappings against actual HTTP responses (permanent 301/308 redirects for genuine moves, appropriate 404/410 for removals), relevant final destinations, canonical/indexing directives, updated internal links and sitemaps, and absence of redirect loops or irrelevant homepage redirects; retain migration redirects for at least one year where feasible, longer when practical.

Frontend Checks#

Apply to browser-based, mobile-web, embedded, or other user-facing interfaces. Record N/A with reasons for headless services.

Reference basis: Google Search Central — JavaScript SEO basics; Google Search Central — Structured data introduction; Google Search Central — Search appearance guidance.

  • SEO-061 Verify important textual content and links are present in the rendered DOM as seen by search crawlers.

  • SEO-062 Use standard <a href> links for navigation; test crawlable routes, deep links, and refresh behavior.

  • SEO-063 Render unique page titles, meta descriptions, canonical tags, and heading structure for each indexable view.

  • SEO-064 Check that meta robots directives are correct in the initial document and are not accidentally inherited from staging.

  • SEO-065 Keep URL changes, history navigation, canonical URLs, and visible content synchronized for single-page apps.

  • SEO-066 Validate JSON-LD, microdata, or RDFa against visible page content and supported Google features.

  • SEO-067 Use semantic headings, clear labels, descriptive image alt text, and accessible main navigation.

  • SEO-068 Ensure lazy-loaded content and images become discoverable without requiring a user scroll/click for essential text.

  • SEO-069 Measure field Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) and mobile UX on important page templates.

  • SEO-070 Reserve dimensions for media and dynamic components to minimize layout shift.

  • SEO-071 Verify responsive rendering, viewport settings, and content readability on small screens.

  • SEO-072 Check error, empty, and not-found UI states do not misleadingly present a successful indexable page.

  • SEO-073 Test locale switching and alternate language navigation without duplicating canonical targets.

  • SEO-074 For indexable paginated collections, give each page a distinct crawlable URL and a justified canonical target; verify linked page sequences without relying on rel="next"/rel="prev" as Google indexing signals.

  • SEO-075 Where image or video discovery matters and ordinary links are insufficient, assess image/video sitemap extensions, media URL access, metadata accuracy, and submission or validation without assuming sitemap inclusion guarantees indexing.

  • SEO-076 For businesses with multiple physical locations, verify each genuinely distinct location has an accurate, useful landing page and consistent name, address, contacts, hours, and applicable LocalBusiness data across the site and maintained listings.

  • SEO-077 On sites accepting public user-generated or paid outbound links, verify provenance-appropriate rel="ugc", rel="sponsored", or rel="nofollow" attributes without indiscriminately marking ordinary editorial links.

  • SEO-078 For public sites, verify the declared favicon/icon URL resolves, uses an appropriate supported format and caching behavior, and displays as intended in relevant browsers and search surfaces without treating the icon as a ranking guarantee.

  • SEO-079 For sites with related native applications, validate Apple Universal Links or Android App Links, allowed URL associations, appropriate app-promotion surfaces, and usable browser fallbacks where relevant.

  • SEO-080 For pages shared through social platforms, validate real destination previews for title, description, URL, and image with supported Open Graph/platform metadata without claiming direct ranking benefits.

  • SEO-081 If long-term ownership, branding, or portability matters, choose and document an appropriate controlled domain; verify DNS, HTTPS, preferred host, canonical URLs, and a redirect/URL-mapping plan for any migration from a platform subdomain. Do not claim a custom TLD or hosting suffix directly improves ranking.

  • SEO-082 Where off-site discovery is relevant, verify that research and outreach for editorial roundups, original statistics with disclosed methods, useful free tools, journalist requests, unlinked mentions/source credits, relevant broken-resource replacements, author-approved visual/video contributions, real vendor case studies, and eligible listings have distinct reader value. In relevant forums and communities, contribute useful first-hand answers under each community's rules, transparently disclose any material product affiliation, and add links only when genuinely allowed and helpful; do not game karma or mass-post. Validate facts, rights and destination URLs, respect independent publisher choice and disclosure/link attributes, and log only confirmed placements and referrals; reject paid, automated, coercive or excessive reciprocal link schemes and any guaranteed backlink, rank or AI-citation claims.

Release gate#

  • All applicable high-priority checks above pass, or an authorized decision-maker has explicitly accepted and documented each residual risk.
  • Failed items have tracked remediation, owners, and deadlines; material blockers remain blocked until resolved.
  • Evidence links and the reviewer, review date, and final decision are recorded.

Domain-specific approval rule: Do not sign off if important production pages are unintentionally blocked, canonicalized away, broken, or missing essential content. Search ranking is not guaranteed.

Trusted references and scope#

The checks above are adapted into practical verification questions from these authoritative publications (not copied as standards text). Verify current versions and the project's scope before sign-off.

  • Google Search Central — JavaScript SEO basics
  • Google Search Central — Structured data introduction
  • Google Search Central — Supported structured-data features — distinguish Schema.org validity from a currently supported Google Search appearance.
  • Google Search Central — Documentation updates — Google FAQ rich results stopped May 7, 2026; FAQ feature docs were removed in June 2026. Recheck other retired features rather than relying on static skill examples.
  • Google Search Central — Search appearance guidance
  • Google Search Central — AI features and your website
  • web.dev — Core Web Vitals
  • W3C — WCAG 2.2 Overview

Search engines may crawl, render, and index differently. Follow documentation for each target engine; passing these checks cannot guarantee indexing, ranking, or rich results.

  • Google Search Central — Pagination best practices — distinct paginated URLs, canonicals, and obsolete next/prev signals.

  • Google Search Central — Sitemaps overview — optional image/video extensions and discovery limitations.

  • Google Search Central — LocalBusiness structured data — distinct locations and accurate business data.

  • Google Search Central — Qualify outbound links — ugc, sponsored, and nofollow link purposes.

  • Google Search Central — Favicons — icon discovery and eligibility.

  • Primary guidance — current platform-specific configuration and validation.

  • Primary guidance — current platform-specific configuration and validation.

  • Primary guidance — current platform-specific configuration and validation.

  • Google Search Central — Site moves with URL changes — approved old-to-new URL maps, permanent redirects (generally at least one year), sitemaps, crawl/index validation, and post-move monitoring.

  • Google Search Central — SEO starter guide — organize user-relevant topics logically and provide meaningful internal links; no mandatory cluster size or backlink quota.

  • Google Search Central — Link best practices — descriptive, contextual internal links and link attributes.

  • Google Search Central — Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content — original, useful, credible content rather than link manipulation.

  • Google Search Central — Spam policies — manipulative links, site reputation abuse, scaled content abuse and prohibited automated ranking queries; includes updated 2026 enforcement details.

  • Reddit Help — Spam policy — repeated promotion and automated spam prohibited, with individual community rules.

  • Reddit Help — Community moderation — some subreddits use 90/10, others forbid promotion; not a universal rule.

  • Google Search Central — Using the Indexing API — currently supports JobPosting or BroadcastEvent within VideoObject, not general pages; successful notifications do not prove indexing.

  • Chrome for Developers — Agent DevTools configuration — browser access controls and usage-statistics/privacy flags for Chrome DevTools MCP.

  • Google Search Central — Guidance on generative AI content — manual fact-checking and review of AI-generated page text, titles, meta descriptions, structured data and image alt text before publishing; low-value scaled output remains a spam risk.

  • Google Business Profile — Guidelines for representing your business — eligibility and accurate local profile details.

  • Google Business Profile — Manage customer reviews — verified-business review responses where available.

  • Bing Webmaster Tools — Sitemaps — sitemap processing diagnostics.

  • Bing Webmaster Tools — URL inspection — actual crawl and index status.

  • Google Search Central — Preferred Sources publisher guide — eligible domain/subdomain, official opt-in button and deeplink, no guaranteed exposure.

  • Publisher Center — Publication pages update — new Google News Publisher Center registration stopped in 2024.

  • Search Console — RE2 custom filters and query-data limitations — regex filters, anonymization and truncated results.

  • Google Search Central — Robots.txt — crawl disallow is not access control or guaranteed deindexing.

  • Google Search Central — Sitemaps — inclusion is discretionary and lastmod should reflect significant verified changes.

  • Google Search Central — Core Web Vitals — actual LCP, INP and CLS criteria.

  • Google Search Central — Title links — Google may derive result titles from multiple page signals.

  • Google Search Central — Search snippets — no fixed meta-description character limit.

  • Google Search Central — Request a recrawl — quota-limited and not an indexing guarantee.

  • Google RE2 — Syntax — ASCII word boundaries for Search Console regex.

  • Cloudflare — Bot Fight Mode — challenges may affect legitimate clients and crawlers; check actual security events.

  • Google Search Central — JavaScript SEO basics — initial and rendered HTML, correct status and indexing controls.

  • Google Search Central — Software app structured data — conditional rich-result properties and genuine review evidence.

  • Google Search Central — AI features and your website — ordinary Search eligibility and no special AI-only ranking file.

  • IndexNow — FAQ — use only for participating engines, not a general Google indexing mechanism.

  • Google Search Central — Social/video platform properties globally launched July 29, 2026 — supported Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube accounts; Google-side reporting.

  • Google Search Console Help — About platform properties — account/channel ownership, per-platform properties, Google Search/Discover/News reports and limits; data may be partial or require processing.

  • Google Search Central — Analyze social and video content performance — query, post, country, device and timing analysis for verified accounts.

Source review date: 2026-11-14. For a project-specific migration worksheet, see the optional URL map template; do not mark the shared checklist passed based on a plan alone.

Suggested testing tools#

Choose tools appropriate to the project's stack and risks; automation supports evidence but does not approve the checklist.

  • Test focus: crawlability, robots/canonical, rendered metadata, and structured data; include browser and client behavior where applicable.

  • Cross-stack: Lighthouse + Rich Results Test + Google Search Console (URL Inspection and Sitemaps) + Bing Webmaster Tools.

  • Specialized: Schema Markup Validator for schema.org syntax + PageSpeed Insights for field/lab metrics; inspect actual live URLs and representative paginated, media, and regional pages.

  • Python: Beautiful Soup + pytest; for pytest-based suites, run python -m pytest -q.

  • TypeScript: Playwright + schema-dts + Vitest; for Vitest-based suites, run npx vitest run (or npx playwright test for E2E).

  • JavaScript: Playwright + Ajv + Jest; for Jest-based suites, run npx jest --ci (or npx playwright test for E2E).

  • Optional SEO research and validation: Screaming Frog SEO Spider, WebPageTest, Meta Sharing Debugger, Google Trends, and Moz Keyword Explorer. Choose only suitable, maintained tools for the project.

  • Optional crawl/CI toolkit (own or authorized sites only): SEOnaut for self-hosted site crawling, redirect/link and metadata diagnostics (Docker/database required; secure credentials, instance exposure and crawl rate); Unlighthouse for representative multi-page Lighthouse audits (uses sampling, not proof that every URL was tested); lychee for broken links in HTML/Markdown; and Lighthouse CI with a configured lighthouserc and actual CI trigger for repeatable lab checks. An SEO score is not a ranking guarantee or a real-user performance measurement.

  • Conditional agent-connected diagnostics (not required for SEO): Chrome DevTools MCP can inspect an approved, isolated Chrome session, network traffic and performance traces; review which browser data the agent can read/change, disable or disclose usage telemetry where appropriate, and exclude logged-in customer sessions and secrets. Search Console MCP can query owned, authorized GSC/Bing/GA4 properties, but verify OAuth scope, property matching, token storage, optional writes and provider-supported URL submission; do not mistake Indexing API notifications for guaranteed indexing. Inspect the tools and their permissions before installation, and independently validate findings.

  • Optional SEO research platform (not a mandated skill or ranking replacement): OpenSEO offers keyword, backlink, rank and crawl research with hosted, Cloudflare and Docker variants and MCP access. Self-hosted data calls require a paid DataForSEO account and may use additional provider APIs. Register the first admin before exposing the URL publicly, protect credentials/session and agent endpoints, inspect provider/query permissions and hosting limits, and verify measurements against Search Console. An open-source 'Semrush/Ahrefs alternative' description does not establish feature parity or zero cost.

  • Optional Search Console intent research (owned property): Performance → Search results → Add filter → Query → Custom (regex) accepts RE2. The sample ^(?:\S+\s+){7,}\S+$ finds eight-or-more whitespace-separated query tokens; ^(who|what|when|where|why|how|which|can|does|is|should)\s samples selected English question starts. Match each query to its actual landing page, intent and dates; provide a truthful concise answer on the appropriate existing page and review impressions, clicks and CTR. These are not exhaustive (anonymized/truncated queries and language variants), do not prove AI citations or conversion intent, and are not a mandate to create thin FAQ pages or retired Google FAQ rich-result markup. See SEO-002/031/046.

  • Optional earned editorial discovery: Research relevant buyer roundups, journalist requests, original studies with documented sample/method, unlinked factual credits, relevant broken/outdated resource replacements, tested free calculators, consented visual/video explanations, authentic case studies and eligible directories. Obtain independent editor approval, verify rights and claims, prefer permanent accurate URLs, and log actual links/referrals. Restore/redirect your own old URLs only to equivalent successors; avoid manufactured link swaps, automated pitches and guaranteed AI citations. See SEO-082.

  • Optional public competitor-content research: Public /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, accessible subdomains and live pages can suggest incomplete topic/offer leads, not secret plans. Disallow is not a privacy boundary; XML sitemaps are not exhaustive; lastmod does not reliably forecast campaigns, and repeated headlines cannot prove winning A/B tests. Respect content rights and access policies; publish original value rather than copying competitive materials.

  • Optional community-led intent research: Read relevant public Reddit/forum discussions and rules to identify recurring unanswered customer problems; write original, sourced content for owned properties and participate only where you can help. Use an authentic account, accurate affiliation disclosure and community-appropriate links; neither a universal 90/10 posting rule, daily karma schedule nor nofollow/UGC treatment guarantees ranking or AI citations. Do not automate promotional posts, manufacture reviews, disguise link targets, or treat public posts as reusable proprietary copy. See SEO-002/028/077/082.

  • Optional GSC commercial-query research (owned properties only): Performance → Search results → Add filter → Query → Custom (regex). Paste \b(best|vs|versus|alternatives?|pricing|cost|reviews?)\b. This RE2 filter finds selected English comparison/purchase-related words, not customers or guaranteed sales. Inspect the matching page in Pages, SERP context, search appearance, average position, impressions, clicks, CTR, device and dates; change titles only when an accurate improvement serves that page and monitor real outcomes. ASCII word boundaries miss some languages and variants; hidden/anonymized Search Console rows limit completeness. See SEO-014/031.

  • Optional on-page optimization toolkit (source-checked 2026-11-14): Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools for authorized search data; Ahrefs for keyword and content-gap research; Semrush On Page SEO Checker for competitor/page ideas; Yoast SEO and Rank Math for applicable CMS/WordPress work; Surfer Content Editor, MarketMuse Optimize and SE Ranking for optional content/on-page research. Vet plan availability, permitted use, API/AI data sharing, and human sign-off. Proprietary KD, search-volume, content scores and suggested word counts are not Google grading standards; the separately promoted SEO Wins library was unavailable for audit.

  • Optional smaller-site content workflow: Group genuine audience queries by intent into distinctive useful pages; inspect permitted search results and differentiate them with independently fact-checked substance. Use AI as a drafting assistant, not an auto-publisher, and add only contextually useful internal links. Inspect page-specific Search Console evidence after enough data accrues, edit only relevant passages, and optionally request recrawls after meaningful changes. No mandatory KD=0, volume=0–10, 10–15-page batch, 3–5 internal links, fixed title/meta character limits, seven-day loop, 2–5 monthly backlinks, or 3–12-month ranking guarantee. See SEO-002/004/011/014/029/031/082/084.

  • Optional live-site SEO change-monitoring workflow (2026-11-14): Use a stored baseline and a post-release diff for representative and high-traffic production pages, www/preferred-host behavior, response status, X-Robots-Tag, initial/rendered content, canonical, sitemap and robots.txt (including edge/CDN-managed behavior), rather than relying on local source files or a superficial curl -A User-Agent/status-only check. Identify actual WAF challenges, redirect targets, and content served; a spoofable User-Agent string cannot verify a crawler identity. Keep a remediation owner, human approval for destructive/sitewide SEO changes and an actionable rollback. See SEO-086, SEO-029, GEO-079/081, AGENT-043/048.

  • Optional source-reviewed RomeoSEO skills (not installed or independently security-audited): technical-seo-audit, xml-sitemap-check, schema-markup, seo-change-monitor, comparison-page-writer and seo-content-qa are task-specific agent-skill prompts. Verify their current content and scripts before running them, restrict filesystem/network/CMS permissions, and treat all numeric audits and pass scores as unverified until measured against your own site. Tool use is optional; prefer observed URLs, response evidence, accessible content, genuine reviews, accurate vendor pricing/date and human editorial approval. Do not use these skills to install or publish automatically.

  • Optional social-post Google Search discovery workflow (reviewed 2026-11-14): For a creator/business that controls a supported public Instagram, TikTok, X or YouTube account, use Search Console → property selector → Add property → supported platform → complete account/channel verification (or select an already connected property). Analyze genuine query–post pairs, impressions, clicks and other Google-side performance across the actually available Google Search surfaces, then use audience intent and independent fact-checking to inform helpful, platform-native titles/captions and distribution. Google announced global access on 2026-07-29, but still verify the actual account and report availability; new properties can show partial/initially empty data. This does not measure all social-platform views, guarantee post indexing or make a keyword at the beginning mandatory. Separate Google clicks from platform engagement, site referrals and actual sales. See SEO-087, SEO-002/028/031.

  • Actionable Search Console content-opportunity worksheet (owned properties): Export a dated page–query sample, group queries by actual intent, and compare impressions, clicks, CTR, position and destination URL. Optionally use the existing question, eight-token and commercial-word regex samples. Select one relevant page and make a specific improvement: a clear first-paragraph answer, accurate comparison, better internal link or descriptive title that matches the page. Record the old text, update date, and observed results; never infer purchases solely from query wording. Maps to SEO-002/004/011/014/031.

  • Ethical decision-page and first-hand research workflow: Start with genuine buyer questions from product support, search data or customer feedback; inspect permitted public search results for the type of answer people need. Consolidate overlapping queries into one useful page, test competing solutions or a free calculator with unusual input cases, publish original examples/limitations and cite dated, source-checked pricing. Add only relevant internal links and appropriate schema. Revisit for factual changes instead of using a keyword-density, page-count, title-length or weekly-publication target. Maps to SEO-002/003/004/011/014/018/028/034/084.

  • Editorial coverage and community workflow: Find accurate category roundups, unlinked credits, active public forum discussions, journalist questions, genuine vendor case-study opportunities and relevant organizations/directories. Contribute a distinct original statistic, tested product example, permissioned diagram/video, or useful explanation; send targeted, low-pressure messages and maintain factual publisher entries with editor consent. Follow forum rules, disclose affiliation and log live references and actual referrals separately from AI mentions. Maps to SEO-028/031/077/082/083.

  • Public competitive-content research, limited to accessible pages: Review public navigation, published comparison pages, sitemaps and robots rules to find topical gaps worth answering independently. Record the exact source and date, and treat URL prefixes and repeated headlines as observations rather than proof of private marketing plans or conversion experiments; never try to bypass access controls or copy protected assets. Maps to SEO-002/003/007/009/028/082.

  • Social and video discoverability: On supported accounts the owner controls, review Search Console platform-property post/query reports, and compare them with native analytics and actual referrals. Publish useful platform-specific descriptions, accessible subtitles/transcripts and real demos where audience interest supports them. A post's position in Google Search is a result to measure, not an outcome created merely by adding an account, putting a term first or sharing. Maps to SEO-020/030/031/080/087.

  • Evidence: Save tool versions, configuration, test environment, fixtures, results, and links in project-specific review records using the existing checklist IDs. Expert review remains necessary where relevant.

Suggested AI skills for verification#

These are optional agent review aids, not automated passes or release approval. Each linked repository had at least 1,000 GitHub stars when checked on 2026-11-12; counts are per repository, not per skill, and do not indicate security or correctness.

  • seo-audit — Review crawlability and on-page SEO (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • schema — Inspect structured-data markup and current search-feature eligibility (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • programmatic-seo — Examine data-source provenance, real per-page value, template rendering, missing data, canonical/indexing signals and scaled-page quality before launch (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • site-architecture — Check navigation and indexable URL structure (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).

Additional optional editorial aid (verified 2026-11-14, not installed): Claude Blog can assist with source research, drafting, link/fact-checking and Markdown/HTML/PDF review. Its automated five-gate workflow and 0–100 score are not independent editorial approval or evidence of Google rankings/AI citations. Claude Code/model access may cost money; optional image/narration APIs can incur charges and some fallback searches share topic metadata externally. Check permitted data flows, source and image rights, installer/uninstaller behavior, exact pinned release/commit, and human sign-off under SEO-004/028/084 before publishing. The upstream README warns about a destructive v2.2.0 uninstaller; use a reviewed safe version, not an unchecked older script.

Additional source-reviewed SEO agent references (2026-11-14; NOT installed or part of the curated 2026-11-12 skill recommendations): Claude SEO is an optional Claude Code audit plugin for technical, content, schema, local SEO and GEO research; Agency Agents — Marketing SEO Specialist is a customizable reviewer-role prompt, not a standalone testing tool. Treat Claude SEO as a non-endorsed, separately risk-reviewed aid (see the informational risk register), not as an automatic fix/publish workflow. Before any use, inspect the pinned source, installer and tool permissions, browser/network access, credentials, model/API recipients and costs. Independently substantiate findings against SEO-004/018/029/031/084 and actual owner-account/URL diagnostics; vendor traffic, ranking and audit scores are not proof of search results or release approval.

How to check: In a project-specific copy, have the agent audit the frontend scope and map findings to this file's existing checklist IDs, with code/configuration references, reproducible test results, failed or inapplicable cases, and uncertainties. Independently verify findings; keep shared template boxes unchecked and retain human approval requirements.

Before use: Read the skill's SKILL.md, referenced scripts, license, and requested tool permissions. Only execute vetted skills with appropriate access in a controlled environment.

Important warning: reference only#

⚠️ Reference only — not a definitive or exhaustive checklist. This template is a starting point for review, not the ultimate authority or a guarantee of project safety, quality, regulatory compliance, accessibility, security, or launch readiness.

Use project-specific judgment and independent verification. Requirements and risks evolve and differ by project, technology, and jurisdiction. Adapt the checks, consult current authoritative sources, perform relevant tests, and obtain qualified specialist review or approval when appropriate. Checking every box does not replace these steps.

Reference, not a certification. Check applicability, verify important claims against current primary sources, and seek expert review where necessary. Suggest an improvement.
